findings.asked: Expand with Pascal's triangle; P(no red); P(at least 2 red).
findings.wentWrong: Pascal's triangle not written (a mark lost); expansion to the wrong power or with signs missing; P(0) subtracted from 1 or p and q swapped; 'at least 2' needed 1 - {P(0) + P(1)} - many computed P(2) only or rounded early.
findings.rule: At least r: 1 minus the probabilities of fewer than r, in brackets.

findings.wentWrong: 0.3 and 0.7 mixed; the coefficient 4 omitted; 'at least' forgotten.
findings.rule: Each term = coefficient x p to the r x q to the n - r.

findings.asked: Exactly two sixes; at least two.
findings.wentWrong: 0.2 and 0.8 mixed; the 10 omitted; brackets missing in 1 - (P(0) + P(1)); coefficients left out of the complement.

findings.asked: Selected terms of an expansion; 'at least'.
findings.wentWrong: Wrong terms selected; 'at least' misunderstood; a simple p cubed overcomplicated; truncation to 0.03.
findings.rule: Match the term to the number of successes; do not truncate.

findings.asked: Pascal's triangle; a chosen term; 'at least'.
findings.wentWrong: Many summed several terms instead of using 1 minus two terms and made errors; calculator statistics functions without working scored nothing.
findings.rule: Use the complement when it is shorter, and show the terms.

ruleToRemember: Identify n and p (success as the question defines it), q = 1 - p; P(X = r) = coefficient x p to the r x q to the n - r with the coefficient from Pascal's triangle; 'at least r' = 1 - (P(0) + ... + P(r - 1)) in brackets; round only at the end.
aStarSignal: Choosing the complement route for 'at least' and writing every term with its coefficient before evaluating.
